decisions.reason: The name, professional description, and all listed denials are supported by the source.
The Harbor Tools role and dates, both personally built tools, training, and listed skills and achievements are supported by the source.

The record claims Dispatch Loom was not sold to external customers, but the source asks to distinguish operational use from a product sold to external customers; it does not explicitly establish that the tool was not sold.
The separate SQL handover checklist, personal build and handover documentation, and absence of a measured impact are supported.
The reconciliation-time result, six-run measurement, three-hour weekly difference, team attribution, and Ada’s stated contribution are supported.
The workshops, handbook and five examples are supported. The record also correctly preserves the conflict between the recalled count of 12 and the attendance sheet’s 14.
The source supports Python use to write the Dispatch Loom parser.
The source supports SQL use for Dispatch Loom checks and the Roster Note checklist, as well as extensive SQL use.
The source supports using PostgreSQL for the production database.
The source supports using Git for version control.
The source supports personally training dispatch coworkers in workshops.
The source supports gathering Dispatch Loom requirements from warehouse supervisors.
